extracted.intended_audience: applicants, licensees, parties, attorneys, and state/local officials participating in NRC construction permit/combined license/limited work authorization proceedings and formal adjudications
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements and procedural standards governing acceptance/docketing, notices, early partial decisions on site suitability, limited work authorizations, subpoenas, expert examination, and required discovery disclosures in NRC licensing and adjudicatory proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completeness determination timeframe and notice of deficiencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Each part of an application will be initially treated as tendered; if determined incomplete, the Director will inform the applicant of the determination and the respects in which the document is deficient; such a determination will generally be made within 30 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: "Each part of an application submitted ... will be initially treated as a tendered application. If it is determined that any one of the parts ... is incomplete and not acceptable for processing, the Director ... will inform the applicant of this determination and the respects in which the document is deficient. Such a determination of completeness will generally be made within a period of 30 days."

rubrics_metrics.name: Part one completeness requirements (construction permit / combined license)
rubrics_metrics.description: Part one of an application will not be considered complete unless it contains proposed findings required by §2.101(a-1)(1)(i) and describes the applicant's site selection process, specifies the extent of consideration of alternative sites, explains relationship to early review application, and briefly describes long-range plans for ultimate development of the site.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to construction-permit and combined-license applications; upon assignment of docket number, follow procedures in §2.101(a)(3) and (4) for formal docketing and distribution of copies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Docketing of additional parts upon completeness determination
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional parts of the application will be docketed upon a determination by the Director that they are complete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is applied after part one is accepted; the Director determines completeness of part two and later parts before docketing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of docketing content and publication requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: If part one is docketed, the Director must publish in the Federal Register and send to the Governor (or appropriate State official) a notice of docketing stating the purpose of the application, the location of the proposed site, that a notice of hearing will be published, and request comments within a specified period (commonly 120 days or 60 days depending on procedure).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For early site review (construction/combined license) the notice requests comments within 120 days or such other time as specified. For limited work authorization notices, comments must be submitted within 60 days or other time specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of hearing modified to limited issues (site suitability)
rubrics_metrics.description: When an applicant requests early review/hearing and early partial decision on site suitability, the notice of hearing must be modified so the matters of fact and law to be considered relate only to the site suitability issues under review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: "Where an applicant ... requests an early review and hearing and an early partial decision on issues of site suitability ... the provisions in the notice of hearing ... shall be modified so as to relate only to the site suitability issue or issues under review."

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary notice of hearing after docketing part two
rubrics_metrics.description: After docketing of part two, a supplementary notice of hearing must be published regarding remaining unresolved issues; it must provide that any person whose interest may be affected and who desires to participate as a party shall file a petition for leave to intervene pursuant to §2.309 within the time prescribed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The supplementary notice also must provide appropriate opportunities for an interested State representative under §2.315(c) and for limited appearances under §2.315(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuation as party after initial site-suitability hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: A person permitted to intervene under the initial notice of hearing on site suitability who was not dismissed or did not withdraw may continue as a party on remaining issues only if, within the time prescribed in the supplementary notice, they file a notice of intent to continue with a supporting affidavit identifying the specific aspects they wish to continue on and setting forth with particularity the basis for their contentions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A non-timely notice may lead to dismissal unless the party makes a substantial showing of good cause for failure to file on time, with reference to factors in §2.309(c)(1)(i)-(iv) and (d); the notice will be ruled upon by the Commission or presiding officer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preservation of board/presiding officer membership
rubrics_metrics.description: To the maximum extent practicable, the membership of any Atomic Safety and Licensing Board (or presiding officer) designated to preside on remaining unresolved issues will be the same as that designated for the initial notice of hearing on site suitability issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to continuity of adjudicatory panels between initial and supplemental proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit on multiple pre-part-two reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission will not conduct more than one review of site suitability issues with regard to a particular site prior to filing and review of part two of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This prevents repeated early-site-suitability reviews prior to submission of full information in part two.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commission discretion to decline early hearing or early partial decision
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission, on its own initiative or upon motion filed at least 60 days before commencement of evidentiary hearing, may decline to initiate an early hearing or render an early partial decision on site suitability issues under specified circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two primary bases: (1) where no partial decision comparing proposed and alternative sites is requested, if further review likely would identify preferable alternative sites and the partial decision would lead to irreversible commitment of resources prejudicing later review; (2) where an early partial decision would not be in the public interest considering (i) likelihood early findings would retain validity later, (ii) objections of cognizant State/local agencies, and (iii) possible effect on the public interest and parties of an early, possibly non-conclusive, resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of other decision-related sections to partial initial decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Provisions of §§2.331, 2.339, 2.340(b), 2.343, 2.712, and 2.713 apply to any partial initial decision rendered in accordance with this subpart; §2.340(c) (or 2.340(c) as applicable) does not apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No construction permit or combined license may be issued without completion of the full NEPA review (Section 102(2)) and subpart A of part 51. The Commission's authority to review a partial initial decision sua sponte, or to raise sua sponte an unraised issue, will be exercised within the same time as for a full decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partial decision content requirements (site identification and need for further information)
rubrics_metrics.description: A partial decision on one or more site suitability issues must clearly identify the site to which it applies and indicate to what extent additional information may be needed and additional review may be required to enable the Commission to determine whether a construction permit (or combined license) for the site should be issued or denied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures partial decisions specify their scope and the remaining informational/review needs for ultimate licensing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duration and reopening of partial decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: A partial decision remains in effect for 5 years, or where the applicant has made timely submittal of required supporting information, until the proceeding for a permit/combined license on the site is concluded, unless significant new information substantially affecting earlier conclusions is found and the hearing record is reopened; upon good cause, the Commission may extend the 5-year period for up to 1 year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The partial decision can be reopened sua sponte or on motion if significant new information exists; duration adjustments depend on timely submission of later application parts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation and finality of partial decisions in combined-license proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Partial decisions on site suitability issues in a combined license proceeding shall be incorporated into the decision regarding issuance of a combined license and treated as resolved those matters resolved in connection with the partial decision; an adverse decision results in denial without prejudice for resubmission, with resubmitted application completeness review addressing matters identified as bases for denial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also, while a partial decision is in effect, the Commission may not modify, rescind, or impose new requirements within its scope unless necessary for compliance with the Commission's regulations in effect at the time of the partial decision, or to assure adequate protection of public health/safety or common defense and security (subject to 10 CFR 2.758 exception).

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing fees for applications with limited work authorization requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Each application that contains a request for limited work authorization must be accompanied by any fee required by §50.30(e) and part 170 of this chapter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fee requirements are mandatory at time of filing such requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Part one completeness for limited work authorization applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Part one of an application for limited work authorization will not be considered complete unless it contains the information required by §50.10(d)(3) or §53.1130(a)(3) as applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upon assignment of a docket number, the procedures in §2.101(a)(3) and (4) relating to formal docketing and submission/distribution of additional copies must be followed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of docketing and comment period for limited work authorizations
rubrics_metrics.description: If part one of a limited work authorization application is docketed, the Director will publish in the Federal Register and send to the Governor a notice of docketing that states the purpose and location and requests comments on the limited work authorization; the notice will state that comments must be submitted to the NRC within 60 days or such other time as specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Similarly, when part two is docketed, a notice requesting comments on the construction permit or combined license will be published with a 60-day comment period unless another period is specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of hearing content for limited work authorizations
rubrics_metrics.description: The notice of hearing on part one of the application must set forth the matters of fact and law to be considered and be modified to state that the hearing will relate only to matters related to §§50.33(a)-(f), 53.1109, and 53.1306(a) or §53.1413 as applicable, and the limited work authorization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supplementary notices and intervention opportunities mirror the broader site-suitability process; petitions to intervene must meet subpart C requirements including §2.309.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on issuing limited work authorizations before NEPA review
rubrics_metrics.description: A limited work authorization may not be issued under §50.10(d) or §53.1130(a) without completion of the review for limited work authorizations required by subpart A of part 51.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Partial initial decisions for limited work authorizations are subject to the same provisions as other partial decisions and the Commission's authority to review sua sponte applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of Subpart G (formal adjudications)
rubrics_metrics.description: Subpart G applies to and supplements subpart C with respect to specified enforcement proceedings, proceedings for initial licensing of a uranium enrichment facility, proceedings related to nuclear power reactor licenses/permits, proceedings for high-level radioactive waste repository initial applications, and other proceedings as ordered by the Commission; where conflict exists with subpart C, subpart G controls.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subpart G applies when the presiding officer finds resolution of contentions requires resolution of issues of material fact where credibility or motive/intent are at issue, among other specified circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions for military or foreign affairs functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Consistent with 5 U.S.C. 554(a)(4), the Commission may provide alternative procedures in adjudications to the extent they involve the conduct of military or foreign affairs functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a limited exception to normal adjudicatory procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subpoena issuance and relevance showing
rubrics_metrics.description: On application by any party, the designated presiding officer (or Chief Administrative Judge if unavailable) will issue subpoenas requiring attendance/testimony or production of evidence; the issuing officer may require a showing of general relevance of the testimony/evidence and may withhold the subpoena if such a showing is not made; the officer may not determine admissibility of evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subpoenas must bear the Commission's name, issuing officer, and hearing title; advise of quashing procedure. Service rules: must be served by a non-party ≥18 years old unless acknowledged or served by Commission employee; fees/mileage tendered (except for subpoenas issued on behalf of the Commission); proof of service filed. Failure to make proof does not affect validity. Motion to quash or modify allowed if subpoena is unreasonable or requires irrelevant evidence; Commission may condition denial of motion on just and reasonable terms. Commission will seek judicial enforcement on application for subpoenas issued to a party that have not been quashed. Paragraphs (a)-(g) not applicable to attendance/testimony of Commissioners or NRC personnel or to records in their custody.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination by qualified experts
rubrics_metrics.description: A party may request permission for a qualified individual with scientific/technical training to participate in examination and cross-examination of expert witnesses; the presiding officer may permit such participation upon finding that (1) cross-examination by that individual would further the proceeding, (2) the individual is qualified by training/experience, (3) the individual has read the written testimony and documents to be used, and (4) the individual has prepared and submitted a cross-examination plan in accordance with §2.711(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examination/cross-examination must be limited to areas within the individual's expertise. The party and their attorney remain responsible for the conduct of the examination/cross-examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discovery — initial disclosures of persons and documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as otherwise stipulated or ordered, a party other than the NRC staff must, without awaiting a discovery request, provide: (1) names and contact info of individuals likely to have discoverable information relevant to disputed issues alleged with particularity in the pleadings and identify subjects of information; and (2) a copy or description by category and location of all documents/data/tangible things in the party's possession, custody, or control that are relevant to disputed issues alleged with particularity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a required document is publicly available (e.g., on NRC website or Public Document Room), sufficient disclosure is the location, title, and page reference. These disclosures must be made within 45 days after issuance of a prehearing conference order following the initial prehearing conference specified in §2.329, unless otherwise stipulated or ordered. Duty of disclosure is continuing: updates must be made every month after initial disclosures on a due date selected by the presiding officer unless parties agree otherwise. Updates limited to documents subject to disclosure and need not include documents developed/obtained/discovered during the two weeks before the due date. Disclosure duty ends when the presiding officer issues a decision resolving that disputed issue or at another time specified by the presiding officer or Commission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discovery — disclosure of expert testimony and required written report contents
rubrics_metrics.description: In addition to initial disclosures, a party (other than NRC staff) must disclose the identity of any person who may be used at trial to present evidence under §2.711 and, except in proceedings with pre-filed written testimony, must accompany that disclosure with a written, signed report by the witness containing: complete statement of all opinions and basis/reasons, data/information considered, any exhibits to be used as summary/support, witness qualifications including publications in past 10 years, and listing of other cases where the witness testified at trial or by deposition in the past 4 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These disclosures must be made at times and in sequence directed by the presiding officer; absent directions or stipulation, disclosures must be made at least 90 days before hearing commencement or presentation date. If the evidence is intended solely to contradict or rebut evidence identified by another party under paragraph (b)(2), disclosures must be made within 30 days after disclosure by the other party.
